notes: The Recreation and Park Commission's 1961 volume, thinner on construction than the 1950s: most contracts now went through the Department of Public Works. Curated: namings (Di Massimo bocce courts, Lazzeri diamond), the Lake Merced launching facility, and dedications at Helen Wills and Midtown Terrace.

coverage.remaining: Routine items (painting, floodlights, roofing, Aquatic Park bocce phase II, Mission Pool) not curated. The Yerba Buena Senior Center dedication has no page.

findings.address_as_written: North Beach Playground, J. J. Di Massimo Bocci Ball Courts
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission named the new bocce courts at North Beach Playground, two regulation courts and a short court that the maintenance staff had built cheaply for the district's elderly Italian residents, for J. J. Di Massimo, the playground's gardener, who had pressed for them for years.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, January 12, 1961, Resolution No. 4263

findings.address_as_written: Lake Merced boat launching facility, beside the Aquatic Center Building
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract for the 1955 bond program's boat launching facility at Lake Merced, moved beside the Aquatic Center Building from a first site too near the gun clubs, to the Duncanson-Harrelson Co.; the lake then had some 287 sailboats and was the Sea Scouts' headquarters.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, February 2, 1961
